RFC 9293 requires simultaneous open; the state is not restricted to waiting for SYN+ACK.
corrections.before: The TCP state of a client that has sent its SYN and is waiting for SYN+ACK.
corrections.after: A TCP state waiting for a matching connection request after sending an active-open SYN. An ordinary client expects SYN+ACK, but simultaneous open can first receive a SYN and enter SYN-RECEIVED.

corrections.reason: RFC 9293 SYN-RECEIVED is not exclusively a server state.
corrections.before: The TCP state of a server that has received a SYN and replied with SYN+ACK, waiting for the final ACK: a half-open connection.
corrections.after: A TCP state waiting for acknowledgement after both receiving and sending a connection request. It commonly follows a server SYN+ACK but can also arise from simultaneous active opens.

corrections.reason: The former browser-close example did not establish which endpoint closed first.
corrections.before: After the browser closes its side, it waits in LAST_ACK for the server's ACK.
corrections.after: After first receiving and acknowledging a peer FIN, an endpoint sends its own FIN and waits in LAST_ACK for its acknowledgement.

corrections.reason: Avoid promising universal three-to-one RTT costs.
corrections.before: Reusing a connection turns a three-round-trip HTTPS fetch into a one-round-trip one.
corrections.after: In an ideal fresh TCP plus full TLS 1.3 example, setup and one request/response take three RTTs; an already usable connection can reduce that example to one RTT.

corrections.reason: Avoid claiming every congestion controller never grows its window when application-limited.
corrections.before: When a sender has less data to send than its window allows, so its rate is set by the application rather than by congestion control. Algorithms avoid growing the window from such periods.
corrections.after: A sending period constrained by available application data rather than by the transport’s current sending allowance. Congestion-control algorithms have specific rules for such periods; CUBIC excludes application-limited time from its cubic epoch and BBRv1 guards against misleading low delivery-rate samples.

corrections.reason: Physical link rate alone does not exclude receive/congestion-window constraints.
corrections.before: A video call sending 2 Mbit/s over a 100 Mbit/s path is application-limited.
corrections.after: An application producing 2 Mbit/s while the transport can currently send faster is application-limited; a 100 Mbit/s link alone would not establish that allowance.

corrections.reason: Do not imply ECN/AQM-capable CUBIC must wait for overflowing buffers.
corrections.before: Congestion control that treats lost packets (and ECN marks) as its main signal to slow down, as Reno and CUBIC do. It tends to fill router buffers before reacting.
corrections.after: Congestion control that uses packet loss as a congestion signal, as Reno and CUBIC do; ECN can signal the response before a drop. A saturated flow with a large unmanaged tail-drop queue can build a standing backlog, but queue growth depends on AQM, feedback and other limits.

corrections.reason: Remove universal grows-until-overflow example.
corrections.before: CUBIC keeps growing until a buffer overflows, so a loss-based flow builds queues.
corrections.after: A continuously backlogged CUBIC flow can build a standing queue at a tail-drop bottleneck; ECN/AQM and sender limits can change the outcome.

corrections.reason: The old example contradicted the precise definition by claiming halving on every loss.
corrections.before: Reno's window traces a sawtooth: climb by one segment per round trip, halve on each loss.
corrections.after: In the ideal congestion-avoidance model, Reno grows by about one segment per RTT and roughly halves its full-flight window on a qualifying fast-recovery event; timeouts differ.

corrections.reason: Separate a bounded illustrative sawtooth from all Reno loss behaviour.
corrections.before: The shape of Reno's congestion window over time: a steady climb of one segment per round trip, then a sudden halving at each loss, repeated.
corrections.after: The repeated rise and fall of a congestion window. In the ideal Reno congestion-avoidance illustration, linear growth alternates with halving on a qualifying loss event; timeouts, different algorithms and unequal cycles change that shape.

corrections.reason: Delayed and cumulative ACKs invalidate the former unqualified one-ACK-one-packet example.
corrections.before: If ACKs arrive every millisecond, an ACK-clocked sender releases a segment every millisecond.
corrections.after: Under a one-full-segment-per-ACK teaching model with open windows and ready data, an ACK every millisecond can permit a segment every millisecond; ACKs need not correspond one-to-one to segments.

corrections.reason: RFC 8257 defines DCTCP feedback separately; L4S is an architecture, not an algorithm that mandates original DCTCP use AccECN.
corrections.before: Accurate ECN: a TCP feedback scheme, standardised as RFC 9768 in 2026, that lets the receiver report how many packets (and bytes) were CE-marked, rather than classic ECN's single on/off signal per round trip. Algorithms such as DCTCP and L4S need this finer feedback.
corrections.after: Accurate ECN: TCP feedback specified in RFC 9768 (2026), using a small cumulative CE-packet counter and optional byte counters for the received ECN codepoints. It supports finer feedback than classic RFC 3168; original DCTCP uses its own modified ECE signalling and does not require AccECN.

corrections.reason: Distinguish RFC 9000 establishment address validation from migration path challenge.
corrections.before: Checking that a peer can really receive packets at a new address, by sending a random challenge it must echo, before trusting that path.
corrections.after: QUIC’s PATH_CHALLENGE/PATH_RESPONSE exchange tests reachability on a path using unpredictable echoed data. It is one form of address validation; connection establishment can validate an address through handshake or token rules instead, and sending on an unvalidated path is restricted.

corrections.reason: Define the space concept actually captured by its aliases.
corrections.before: A counter identifying a QUIC transmission within one packet-number space; newly transmitted packets use new increasing numbers, even when carrying previously sent stream data. Initial, Handshake and Application Data use separate spaces.
corrections.after: A counter identifying a QUIC transmission within one packet-number space; a new transmission uses a new increasing number even when resending stream data. A packet-number space is a separate numbering and acknowledgement context: Initial, Handshake and Application Data use three such spaces.

corrections.reason: The backlog/rate rule requires the FIFO/fixed-rate assumptions already present in the lesson.
corrections.before: Time a packet spends waiting in a buffer behind other packets before it can be sent. It is the backlog ahead divided by the link rate.
corrections.after: Time a packet waits in a queue before its own service starts. For a fixed-rate FIFO with no intervening scheduling changes, its queued work ahead divided by service rate gives that wait; priorities or changing rates require a different model.

corrections.reason: Avoid claiming every packet always sees the full buffer delay.
corrections.before: A 256 KiB buffer on a 2 Mbit/s uplink can add about a second of delay to every packet.
corrections.after: A packet behind 256 KiB in a fixed-rate 2 Mbit/s FIFO waits about a second before its own transmission; other queues or priority classes can differ.

corrections.reason: Do not promise a fixed 95% configuration always moves the bottleneck.
corrections.before: Shaping a home router's uplink to 95% of the modem's rate moves the queue into the router, where fq_codel can manage it.
corrections.after: Shaping below a measured inaccessible bottleneck can move sustained queueing to a controlled router; a suggested 95% setting needs measurement and may not fit variable-rate links.

corrections.reason: NAT compliance does not prescribe universal application keepalive frequency.
corrections.before: RFC 4787 asks that UDP mappings normally last at least two minutes; applications send keepalives more often than that.
corrections.after: RFC 4787 normally requires a UDP mapping timer of at least two minutes; an application chooses keepalive timing for its actual path and requirements rather than assuming all devices meet that minimum.

corrections.reason: Zero-copy/API distinctions already in definition must also hold in example.
corrections.before: send() returns once data is copied into the send buffer, long before the peer receives it.
corrections.after: For an ordinary copied socket send, a returned byte count reports local acceptance into transport buffering; it does not say when the peer receives or processes those bytes.

corrections.reason: Non-blocking describes waiting semantics rather than immediate wall-clock completion of every socket call.
corrections.before: A socket whose calls return immediately: if an operation cannot proceed yet, it raises an error such as BlockingIOError instead of waiting. Event loops use them.
corrections.after: A socket mode in which an operation that cannot progress reports would-block rather than waiting for future data or buffer space. A call can still be partial or fail; CPU work, scheduling and documented platform exceptions mean this is not a promise of zero elapsed time.

corrections.reason: The old main-thread-exits rule was false while another non-daemon thread remains.
corrections.before: A background thread that does not keep a Python program alive: when the main thread exits, daemon threads are stopped.
corrections.after: A Python thread marked so that it does not keep the process alive. The program exits when no non-daemon threads remain, and daemon threads can be stopped abruptly without orderly cleanup.

corrections.reason: Scope abortive behaviour to the actual Linux implementation and final close.
corrections.before: A socket option controlling what close() does with unsent data. With linger enabled and a timeout of 0, close() aborts the connection with RST instead of a graceful FIN.
corrections.after: A socket option controlling close behaviour for pending output. On Linux TCP, enabling linger with a zero timeout requests an abortive close rather than the ordinary graceful FIN exchange; descriptor references and connection state still matter.

corrections.reason: Avoid unsupported blanket claim that no device uses it or that ECN is its direct one-for-one replacement.
corrections.before: A long-deprecated ICMP message by which a router asked a sender to slow down. It was ineffective and is no longer used; ECN replaced the idea with in-band marking.
corrections.after: A deprecated ICMP congestion message. RFC 6633 requires hosts to discard it silently and prohibits routers from originating it; it is distinct from ECN’s in-band packet marking and feedback.

corrections.before: A socket call that receives one datagram and also returns the sender's address, so a single UDP socket can serve many clients and reply to each.
corrections.after: A socket receive call that can also return the sender’s address. On an ordinary UDP socket it consumes at most one datagram, possibly truncating it when the supplied buffer is too small; stream-socket reads have different boundary rules.
corrections.reason: recvfrom is also a valid stream API; scope datagram behaviour explicitly.

corrections.before: A socket call that sends one datagram to an address given in the same call, so an unconnected UDP socket can talk to many peers.
corrections.after: A socket send call that can supply a destination address with the data. On an ordinary unconnected UDP socket it sends one datagram, allowing the socket to address different peers; stream-socket semantics and limits differ.
corrections.reason: sendto is not exclusively a datagram API.

corrections.before: The Python exception (EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK underneath) raised when an operation on a non-blocking socket would have had to wait.
corrections.after: A Python OSError subclass for an operation that cannot complete immediately, including non-blocking socket would-block or connection-in-progress cases. Corresponding error codes include EAGAIN, EWOULDBLOCK, EALREADY and EINPROGRESS.
corrections.reason: Official Python exceptions documentation includes additional in-progress error codes.
asyncio has no top-level asyncio.drain API.

corrections.before: Calling await writer.drain() after each write stops output piling up for a slow reader.
corrections.after: Awaiting writer.drain() after each bounded write makes the coroutine respect transport backpressure; application message sizes and deadlines still need limits.
corrections.reason: Backpressure cooperation is not an unconditional output-memory bound for arbitrary writes.

corrections.before: With a 64 KiB high watermark, asyncio pauses writers once 64 KiB is queued.
corrections.after: With a 64 KiB high watermark, a transport can pause its producer after the buffer exceeds that threshold; one large write can overshoot it.
corrections.reason: A high watermark is not a hard maximum buffer size.

corrections.before: select() on 10,000 sockets rescans all of them on every call.
corrections.after: With the common fd_set interface, select() is limited by FD_SETSIZE (usually 1,024 on Linux); poll() can accept larger descriptor sets but scans the submitted entries.
corrections.reason: The old Linux select(10,000) example exceeds the usual API limit.

corrections.before: With tcp_abort_on_overflow = 0, an overloaded server makes clients wait rather than refusing them.
corrections.after: With tcp_abort_on_overflow = 0, one accept-overflow path can ignore the final ACK and allow later recovery; other overload paths may still drop attempts.
corrections.reason: Do not promise all overloaded clients wait successfully.

corrections.before: HTTP/1.1 headers are framed by a blank line; the body by Content-Length or chunked encoding.
corrections.after: HTTP/1.1 headers end at a blank line; body framing then follows method/status rules, transfer coding, Content-Length or closure.
corrections.reason: Retain body-presence and close-delimiting exceptions in the example too.

splitAuthorCorrections: AIMD/Reno definitions now distinguish FlightSize-based thresholds, temporary recovery inflation and timeout loss windows from a universal halve-on-every-loss story.
RACK, TLP and ProbeRTT definitions no longer imply fixed quarter-RTT/repair/every-ten-second guarantees; versioned eligibility, age, RTT and round conditions are explicit.
TCP half-open now distinguishes pending establishment from the RFC lost-peer-state meaning; simultaneous close is qualified by event order.
EOF/recv and blocking-socket definitions now distinguish positive reads, local receive shutdown, short operations and timeouts.
ServerHello and passive closer no longer open the opposite ClientHello/active-closer definition; three precise new entries cover those and the TCP ACK validity flag.
RTTVAR is a smoothed absolute deviation, not statistical RTT variance; the misleading alias was removed.
HTTP/1.1 no longer implies pipelining is impossible; Content-Length and body-presence exceptions are explicit.
QUIC packet-number spaces, migration conditions and publicly derivable Initial protection are explicit; BBR version-specific details are not generalised to every version.
SO_REUSEADDR, packet pacing, congestion windows and TCP_NODELAY retain implementation/other-sending-rule qualifications rather than promising immediate output or universal reuse.
The IW10 card no longer claims a universal 14,600-byte maximum: the specified max/min rule can exceed that for sufficiently large MSS values.
Compound denominators now include holding-rate and physical-quantity brackets; RTT worked substitutions carry time units; symbolic prose was converted or expressed in plain words.
The question using recv_exact and MAX_MSG was moved to the unit that introduces those helpers; the hard-cap Reno timeout question was moved to its exact trace model.
The Mathis scaling exercise now consistently uses its stated 71 Mbit/s starting value rather than silently substituting 71.2.

gaps: No WAN packet-capture experiment, SYN flood, AQM benchmark or QUIC migration experiment. Source-supported algorithms and explicit bounded models do not imply measured deployment performance.
The selector loop deliberately retains partial-write/would-block defects for its own debugging question; it is not a production server. Services need total deadlines and resource/connection policies.
Advanced UDP options and implementation-specific recovery/state handling are described selectively rather than implementing a full transport stack.
The Chiu/Jain scanned first page/abstract was inspected visually, not a complete independent proof of the paper; the fairness attribution remains limited to its simplified model.

corrections: tcp-udp-header (lesson + tcp-udp-ports-q2): 'Linux UDP normally uses PMTU discovery and can return EMSGSIZE' → Linux's default socket mode (IP_PMTUDISC_WANT) fragments an oversized datagram locally; IP_PMTUDISC_DO returns EMSGSIZE. Verified in a Linux 6.12 container (60,000-byte send: 41 fragments by default; EMSGSIZE with DO/PROBE) and in IP_MTU_DISCOVER(2const); udp(7)'s default-EMSGSIZE sentence is outdated.

tcp-rto-estimator q5: 'samples fall between 98 and 102 ms / swing between 60 and 140 ms' did not determine the stated ≈110/≈260–270 ms RTOs (evenly spread 60–140 ms samples settle near 140–200 ms) → prompt says the samples alternate; worked example says ≈270 ms and notes the spread-sample case.

tcp-slow-start-flights q1: a loss-free switch at 80 segments on a new connection was attributed to ssthresh without explaining where a low ssthresh came from (RFC 5681 starts it arbitrarily high) → worked example names cached/route ssthresh or Linux CUBIC HyStart (sets ssthresh = cwnd).

Linux behaviour was tested on one kernel (6.12, linuxkit) and loopback only; no WAN, AQM, BBR or migration measurements.
QUIC lesson's tuning checklist remains TCP-centric (inherited).
BBRv2/v3 only summarised and hedged; the BBRv3 draft date is time-sensitive (inherited).

Several cross-subject multi-word fallbacks in inherited text still open other subjects' entries ('length field' → security payload-length, 'data byte(s)' → MIDI, 'unsigned integer' → DSA, 'side channels' → crypto, 'error handling' → React try/catch); recorded, not changed.

lowConfidence.claim: Linux default fragments an oversized UDP datagram locally; IP_PMTUDISC_DO returns EMSGSIZE.
lowConfidence.reason: Tested on Linux 6.12 and documented in IP_MTU_DISCOVER(2const), but udp(7) still says EMSGSIZE by default and the behaviour depends on ip_no_pmtu_disc, per-route settings and kernel version; the lesson names the tested kernel.

lowConfidence.claim: q5: a second backend or source address lets the proxy reuse the same source-port pool.
lowConfidence.reason: Tested for Linux connect() and bind-to-source; other operating systems may allocate ephemeral ports globally, which the explanation now notes.

lowConfidence.claim: q5: RTOs settle near 110 ms and 270 ms.
lowConfidence.reason: Re-derived by simulation for the alternating samples now stated in the prompt (108.4–108.7 ms; 268–273 ms).

lowConfidence.claim: q9: sawtooth peaking near 12,000 segments, ≈1 Gbit/s average.
lowConfidence.reason: Idealised steady-state model; assumptions now stated in the worked example; real flows add slow start, timeouts and RTT variation.

lowConfidence.claim: q6: doubling a tail-drop modem buffer roughly doubles queueing delay.
lowConfidence.reason: Holds for one FIFO kept near full by a loss-based sender at a constant uplink rate (now stated); real cable modems may shape or use several queues.

lowConfidence.claim: q1: a loss-free switch to linear growth at 80 segments reflects ssthresh (cached/route value or HyStart).
lowConfidence.reason: HyStart's exit and ssthresh assignment verified in tcp_cubic.c v6.12; a real CUBIC trace would grow cubically, not by exactly one segment, after the switch.

lowConfidence.claim: 25 analogies (mapping and limit).
lowConfidence.reason: Each reviewed against the lesson's primary sources; five corrected. They remain teaching aids, not evidence.

networks/02-ip-routing owns 'rate limiting'/'rate limits'/'rate-limited' on the ICMP-specific icmp-rate-limiting entry; generic uses in tcp-reset-validation, tcp-udp-operational-risks and tcp-bufferbloat-aqm questions open it.
system-design/10-case-studies-1 'state machine' (state-machine-cs1) is the cross-subject fallback for tcp-close-states-production; networks has no TCP-sense entry.

Single-word 'heartbeat(s)' aliases also exist in security/05 and system-design/05; aliases are subject-scoped, and networks/06 uses the word in the same sense as application-heartbeat.

tcp-port-numbers.rationale: Range-count card removed: 28,232 (60,999 − 32,768 + 1) and the ports ÷ hold-time model (≈470/s at 60 s) stay visible in prose, both recomputed. q5 now diagnoses which change adds tuples; tested in a Linux 6.12 container that connect() reuses the same 4 ephemeral ports against a second destination and from a second bound source address, and hedged that other OSes allocate differently. Flats analogy: mapping and the full-tuple/reuse limit are accurate.

questionsRewritten.tcp-udp-ports-q5: Replaced the 470/s calculator with a diagnosis: which change (extra destination/source address, pooling) actually adds connection tuples. Verifier: hedged that Linux connect() reuses the port pool against a new destination (tested) while other systems' allocation differs.

tcp-udp-header.rationale: Both cards (8-byte header; 65,507 = 65,535 − 20 − 8) folded into plain numeric prose (Rule 6). Corrected the Linux oversized-send claim after a container test: the default IP_PMTUDISC_WANT socket fragmented a 60,000-byte datagram into 41 fragments; only IP_PMTUDISC_DO/PROBE returned EMSGSIZE (udp(7)'s 'by default ... EMSGSIZE' wording is outdated). q1 explains header size from services; q2 key (refused or fragmented, all-or-nothing reassembly) holds; 1,480-byte fragment payload checked. Postcard analogy limits (checksum, fragmentation) accurate.

questionsRewritten.tcp-udp-ports-q1: Header-size recall replaced by explaining the size difference from the services each protocol promises.
questionsRewritten.tcp-udp-ports-q2: 65,507-byte arithmetic replaced by predicting local refusal or fragmentation and all-or-nothing reassembly. Verifier: explanation and worked example corrected to Linux's tested default (local fragmentation; EMSGSIZE only with IP_PMTUDISC_DO).

tcp-socket-demultiplexing.rationale: No maths. UDP echo snippet retained (demultiplexing is the objective) and executed on macOS and Linux (b'HELLO'); q4 boundaries 100/200/300 and truncation of an oversized datagram confirmed. Questions unchanged and still answerable. Restaurant analogy: listening socket/accept()/full tuple mapping is fair; limit notes UDP has no accept.

tcp-dns-datagrams.rationale: 1,232 = 1,280 − 40 − 8 kept as a plain numeric sentence with its path assumptions; card removed. TC-bit retry question unchanged and correct. No analogy: a one-question/one-answer exchange is already concrete; a comparison would repeat the postcard picture from tcp-udp-header.

tcp-real-time-transport.rationale: 60 Hz interval card removed; 16.7 ms spacing and ~6 snapshots per 100 ms stay as an illustration. q10 change is workedExample only (formula card → prose, same key). Scoreboard-text analogy maps superseded snapshots and head-of-line blocking; limit covers non-superseded events and media deadlines.

questionsRewritten.tcp-udp-ports-q10: Removed the interval formula from the worked example; reasoning about stream ordering kept.

tcp-udp-operational-risks.rationale: No lesson maths. q9 keeps the forged-source mechanism and states 50 × 100 Mbit/s = 5 Gbit/s in words; every distractor rechecked. Catalogue analogy accurate; the QUIC 3× anti-amplification limit verified in RFC 9000 §8.

questionsRewritten.tcp-udp-ports-q9: Prompt tightened and the rate-multiplication formula card removed; question tests why reflection works.

tcp-handshake-sequence-space.rationale: Header-length and ISN+1 cards folded into prose (15 × 4 = 60 bytes, 40 for options; 1001/5001 trace). The (N + L) mod 2^32 card is reference: useful, but the visible In words line stands alone. q1/q6 changed only in workedExample; 1301/1302 FIN arithmetic rechecked. No analogy: the numbered trace is the mental model; the next lesson carries the handshake analogy.

questionsRewritten.tcp-connections-q1: Formula card removed from worked example; trace reasoning kept.
questionsRewritten.tcp-connections-q6: Formula card removed from worked example; FIN-consumes-one-number reasoning kept.

tcp-handshake-reachability.rationale: No maths, unchanged questions. Phone-line analogy maps the three messages; limit correctly says TCP is not identity proof and must reject old duplicates.

tcp-syn-flood-cookies.rationale: Retry-timing and (A − 1) mod 2^32 cards folded into prose; 1+2+4+8+16 = 31 s and ~63 s match the ip-sysctl tcp_synack_retries text. q7 workedExample-only change rechecked. Analogy corrected: the cloakroom version still stored a coat per customer (per-attempt state), contradicting stateless cookies; rewritten as a stamped ticket that itself carries the party size, with nothing kept at the door.

questionsRewritten.tcp-connections-q7: Modulo formula removed from worked example; mechanism walkthrough kept.

tcp-graceful-close-time-wait.rationale: 2 × MSL card folded into prose (4 min with RFC 793's MSL; Linux TCP_TIMEWAIT_LEN 60 s confirmed in v6.12 tcp.h). q4 workedExample-only change. Phone-goodbye analogy kept; fixed 'the side that hung up first' (contradicted staying on the line) to 'said goodbye first'.

questionsRewritten.tcp-connections-q4: Formula card removed from worked example; both TIME_WAIT purposes explained in prose.

tcp-close-states-production.rationale: No lesson maths. q8 workedExample now reasons in prose: 600 × 60 = 36,000 > 28,232; pool empty after ≈47 s, recomputed. tcp_tw_reuse default 2 rechecked in ip-sysctl. No analogy: the state table and operational checks are procedural; TIME_WAIT already has one in the previous lesson.

questionsRewritten.tcp-connections-q8: Formula card removed from worked example; prediction kept.

tcp-reset-validation.rationale: No maths. q11 workedExample: 2^32 / 2^16 = 65,536 rechecked; reworded 'next expected number', which opened the DSA expected-value entry. Bank call-back analogy maps the exact-match rule and challenge ACK; limit (on-path attacker, RFC 5961 §7 ACK throttling) accurate.

questionsRewritten.tcp-connections-q11: Probability formula card removed from worked example; RFC 5961 rule explained in prose. Verifier: reworded 'next expected number' (opened a DSA expected-value entry).

tcp-byte-sequence-wrap.rationale: Last-byte and wrap-time cards folded into prose; 2^32 × 8 / 10^10 ≈ 3.4 s and ≈0.86 s at 40 Gbit/s recomputed. q1 now tests re-segmented retransmission (ACK 6201); q12 tests why fast wrap needs PAWS. Odometer analogy fair; limit notes timestamp wrap and recent-state only.

questionsRewritten.tcp-reliability-q1: Last-byte arithmetic replaced by predicting how a receiver handles a re-segmented retransmission.
questionsRewritten.tcp-reliability-q12: Wrap-time calculation replaced by explaining why fast wrap is dangerous and which mechanism helps.

tcp-cumulative-ack-model.rationale: No maths. rx() executed on Python 3.14 (macOS) and 3.12 (Linux): output matches the lesson and q4 (501/501/1501/2001, 1001 held once). Serial-story analogy maps cumulative ACK/duplicate ACKs; limit mentions bytes and SACK.

tcp-sack-received-ranges.rationale: Option-length card folded into prose: 2 + 4 × 8 = 34 ≤ 40, five blocks 42, three blocks 26 within the 28 left after timestamps. Questions unchanged. No analogy: the lesson is a short extension of the serial-story picture in the previous unit; another comparison would repeat it.

tcp-rto-estimator.rationale: RTO = SRTT + max(G, 4 RTTVAR) kept essential: it is the RFC 6298 definition the lesson and q5 turn on. EWMA updates are reference with a standalone In words line; 300 → 272.5 ms example recomputed. q5 re-derived by simulation: alternating 98/102 ms settles at ≈108.5 ms, alternating 60/140 ms at 268–273 ms, but evenly spread 60–140 ms samples give only ≈140–200 ms, so the prompt now says the samples alternate and the worked example states that assumption. No analogy: the steady/jittery/slowing-path bullets already give the intuition.

questionsRewritten.tcp-reliability-q5: Replaced the 272.5 ms calculator with a prediction comparing a steady and a jittery path with the same smoothed RTT. Verifier: prompt now says the samples alternate, which the ≈110/≈270 ms figures require.

tcp-rto-backoff-ambiguity.rationale: Geometric-sum card removed; 0.3+0.6+1.2+2.4 = 4.5 s and 'each wait exceeds all previous waits' checked. tcp_retries2 15 ≈ 924.6 s (a lower bound), tcp_rto_max_ms 120,000 and rto_min 200 ms checked in ip-sysctl; TCP_USER_TIMEOUT semantics in tcp(7). q7 workedExample-only; q9 diagnoses the backoff signature. No analogy: a concrete capture signature carries the idea.

questionsRewritten.tcp-reliability-q7: Two-candidate-RTT formula card replaced by prose reasoning.
questionsRewritten.tcp-reliability-q9: Elapsed-time calculator replaced by diagnosing a capture with doubling gaps and predicting what a blocked application experiences.

tcp-fast-retransmit-limits.rationale: Summary/reading only changed; no formulas. Questions unchanged and consistent. No analogy: the duplicate-ACK idea is covered by the serial-story analogy two lessons earlier.

tcp-rack-tail-probes.rationale: PTO = 2 × SRTT card removed; 2 × 40 = 80 ms stated in prose and table (RFC 8985 §7.2). q11 workedExample-only change rechecked against RFC 8985. No analogy: the mechanism table is the clearest summary and the lesson is already dense.

questionsRewritten.tcp-reliability-q11: Formula card removed from worked example; TLP/RACK reasoning extended (why no dup ACKs without the probe).

tcp-receive-window-budget.rationale: A = max(0, min(rwnd, cwnd) − F) kept essential: the new-data budget is the lesson objective and is needed for q11. Example 14,600 − 10,000 = 4,600 bytes and q11's 40 × 1,460 = 58,400 bytes, ≈28 KB budget recomputed. q2 workedExample-only. Kitchen-pass analogy maps rwnd/recv()/backpressure; limit notes delay and the separate congestion window.

questionsRewritten.tcp-flow-control-q2: Formula card removed from worked example.
questionsRewritten.tcp-flow-control-q11: Byte-budget calculator replaced by diagnosing why enlarging rwnd did not raise a cwnd-limited flow's throughput.

tcp-window-throughput-scaling.rationale: X ≤ W / RTT kept essential (objective; q1/q9). BDP = C RTT and W = F × 2^S are reference cards with standalone In words lines. Recomputed: 65,535 B / 0.1 s ≈ 5.24 Mbit/s and ≈52 Mbit/s at 10 ms; 12.5 MB BDP and ≈0.5 %; 65,535 × 2^14 = 1,073,725,440 B; shift 10 ≈ 67 MB, 11 ≈ 134 MB. Conveyor analogy fair; limit notes variable RTT and two windows.

questionsRewritten.tcp-flow-control-q1: 10.5 Mbit/s calculator replaced by predicting how the ceiling changes when RTT rises tenfold.
questionsRewritten.tcp-flow-control-q4: Smallest-shift calculation replaced by the practical consequence that the shift is fixed at the handshake.
questionsRewritten.tcp-flow-control-q9: Formula card removed from worked example; diagnosis unchanged.

tcp-buffer-autotuning.rationale: Card removed; 6,000,000 × 8 / 0.1 = 480 Mbit/s and 10^10 × 0.1 / 8 = 125 MB stated in prose. tcp_rmem default 131,072 and SO_RCVBUF disabling autotuning checked. q7 workedExample-only: 65,536 × 8 / 0.12 ≈ 4.4 Mbit/s. No analogy: a diagnostic checklist lesson; the conveyor analogy in the previous unit already covers windows.

questionsRewritten.tcp-flow-control-q7: Formula card removed from worked example; diagnosis unchanged.

tcp-zero-window-syndrome.rationale: Efficiency (10/(10+40)) and Clark threshold cards removed; prose states four-fifths overhead and min(MSS, half buffer) in words, consistent with RFC 9293 §3.8.6.2.2. Questions unchanged. Warehouse analogy maps zero window, lost window update and persist probes; limit notes exponential probe backoff.

tcp-nagle-delayed-acks.rationale: 41-byte and 2 × RMSS cards removed; RFC 9293 <0.5 s and every-second-segment rule rechecked. Moved the fact that Nagle never holds full-sized segments back into the visible text: the author had placed it only inside the collapsed analogy, and tcp-flow-control-q6 option 1 depends on it. Letters analogy maps Nagle and delayed ACK.

tcp-split-write-latency.rationale: No maths. send_request executed: TCP_NODELAY set and peer received header+body in one read. Questions unchanged. No analogy: the trace diagram is the explanation, and the preceding lesson's letters analogy already sets up the interaction.

tcp-congestion-window-model.rationale: X ≈ cwnd / RTT is reference (the same relationship is essential in tcp-window-throughput-scaling); 100 × 1,460 / 0.05 ≈ 23.4 Mbit/s recomputed. q2 diagnoses a halved rate at constant cwnd (RTT doubled). 1986 32 kbit/s → 40 bit/s collapse inherited from the earlier verified record. Redial analogy fair; limit notes inferred signals and lack of central admission.

questionsRewritten.tcp-congestion-q2: 23 Mbit/s calculator replaced by diagnosing a halved rate at unchanged cwnd (RTT doubled).

tcp-slow-start-flights.rationale: IW formula is reference (RFC 6928 text checked); doubling/segment-count cards removed. q1 key holds, but a new connection normally starts with a very high ssthresh (RFC 5681), so the worked example now explains a loss-free exit at 80 by a cached/route ssthresh or Linux CUBIC HyStart, which sets ssthresh to cwnd (tcp_cubic.c v6.12). Café analogy mapping reworded so leftovers are the signal that ends doubling rather than ssthresh itself.

questionsRewritten.tcp-congestion-q1: cwnd-at-round-4 calculator replaced by reading a cwnd trace and explaining the switch at ssthresh. Verifier: worked example explains how a new connection reaches a low ssthresh without loss.

tcp-aimd-reno-recovery.rationale: AIMD pair is reference; substitution replaced by a duplicate-ACK vs RTO table, checked against RFC 5681 (ssthresh ≤ max(FlightSize/2, 2 SMSS), cwnd = ssthresh + 3 SMSS, LW = 1 SMSS). q4 key and the 0.7 CUBIC distractor rechecked. Road analogy fair; reworded 'Chiu–Jain convergence', which opened a routing-convergence entry.

questionsRewritten.tcp-congestion-q4: Arithmetic prompt replaced by "what does the sender do after three duplicate ACKs" with timeout and CUBIC distractors.

tcp-reno-round-trace.rationale: reno() executed on both platforms; output matches the table, bars and q6 ('4 9 9'). Average-window card replaced by reading guidance (3/4 of peak stated in words). Corrected 'ssthresh is halved' after a timeout (17 → 10 is half the 20-segment window, not half of ssthresh); same wording fixed in q5's explanation. No analogy: tracing the code is the objective.

questionsRewritten.tcp-congestion-q5: Rounds-to-ssthresh calculator replaced by reading a post-timeout trace and explaining the change at 20. Verifier: 'halves ssthresh' corrected to 'sets ssthresh to about half the data in flight'.

tcp-reno-large-path-recovery.rationale: T_rec = (W/2) × RTT is reference; 83,333 segments, 41,667 × 0.1 s ≈ 69 min and RFC 3649's 5 × 10^9 packets / 1⅔ hours checked in the RFC. q9 sawtooth re-derived (peak P with P/2 + 6,000 = P gives 12,000; average 9,000 segments ≈ 1.1 Gbit/s); the worked example now states the steady-loss, fast-recovery-only assumptions. No analogy: the road analogy in tcp-aimd-reno-recovery covers AIMD; this is a scaling consequence.

questionsRewritten.tcp-congestion-q9: 70-minute calculator replaced by explaining why a long fat pipe with occasional loss stays far below capacity. Verifier: worked example states the steady-loss assumptions behind the 12,000-segment sawtooth.

tcp-cubic-time-target.rationale: W(t)/K card is reference; RFC 9438 C = 0.4, β = 0.7. Table recomputed (K = ∛75 ≈ 4.217 s; 70.0, 86.7, 95.6, 100, 102.3, 108.6). q8 trace (cut to 140, K ≈ 5.3 s) consistent. Go-kart analogy fair; limit notes fixed time function and moving share.

questionsRewritten.tcp-congestion-q8: K/W(0) calculator replaced by explaining the plateau near the previous maximum in a trace.

tcp-bbr-versioned-model.rationale: BDP/pacing/cap card is reference; 12.5 MB/s × 0.02 s = 250 KB. BBRv1 constants rechecked in Linux v6.12 tcp_bbr.c (2.885 high gain, 5/4 and 3/4 cycle, cwnd gain 2, 10-round bw filter, 10 s min-RTT window, 200 ms ProbeRTT, 4-packet floor, 3 rounds/25 % startup exit). Removed a duplicated sentence; analogy title aligned with its café-manager text.

tcp-ecn-congestion-feedback.rationale: DCTCP update is reference; RFC 8257 g = 1/16 and cwnd × (1 − α/2) checked. Question unchanged. Sticker analogy: title matched to body; limit extended to on-path devices that clear ECN bits (author's low-confidence item).

tcp-short-transfer-timing.rationale: Round-trip sum card removed (the table totals 5 RTTs); 69 segments in flights 10/20/39 rechecked. q1 diagnoses 3 × 50 ms setup-bound calls; 10 KB fits IW10; serialisation ≈80 µs at 1 Gbit/s. No analogy: counting round trips is a short procedure.

questionsRewritten.tcp-performance-q1: 150 ms timing calculator replaced by choosing which change cuts small-request latency (connection reuse).

tcp-mathis-loss-model.rationale: Mathis approximation kept essential: the square-root law is the objective and q4 supplies it. Derivation and substitution cards removed; 14.2 and 1.42 Mbit/s rechecked; q4 (link capacity absent, <2 % utilisation) and q5 (1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8; 71 → ≈8.9) rechecked. No analogy: the sawtooth explanation is already the intuition.

questionsRewritten.tcp-performance-q4: 71 Mbit/s calculator replaced by predicting the effect of a link upgrade (none) with the model supplied in the prompt.
questionsRewritten.tcp-performance-q5: Specific Mbit/s answer replaced by the proportional factor (an eighth), testing the RTT and square-root relationships.

tcp-bufferbloat-aqm.rationale: Reclassified T_q = Q / R from essential to reference: the sentence before it already states the relationship in words, so seeing the equation is not necessary. 262,144 × 8 / 2 × 10^6 ≈ 1.05 s rechecked. q6 now states the single FIFO queue assumption behind 'roughly doubles'; CoDel q8 control law (interval/√count) matches RFC 8289. Shop-till analogy fair.

questionsRewritten.tcp-performance-q2: Formula card removed from worked example.
questionsRewritten.tcp-performance-q6: 0.4 s calculator replaced by predicting the effect of doubling a modem buffer on a video call. Verifier: prompt states the single FIFO queue assumption.
questionsRewritten.tcp-performance-q8: CoDel control-law formula card replaced by prose.

tcp-stream-blocking-ossification.rationale: No maths; questions unchanged. Checkout-belt analogy maps HTTP/2 head-of-line blocking; QUIC limit (shared congestion and flow control) accurate.

tcp-quic-transport-tradeoffs.rationale: No maths; questions unchanged. Case-reference analogy: connection IDs, path validation and fresh CIDs on a new path checked in RFC 9000 §9.

tcp-socket-calls-backlogs.rationale: No maths; stale introduction fixed by the author is accurate. Questions unchanged. No analogy: a call-by-call table and queue model; the restaurant analogy in tcp-socket-demultiplexing covers listen/accept.

tcp-stream-message-framing.rationale: No maths; questions unchanged. Dictation analogy maps byte stream, invisible send() boundaries, delimiters and length prefixes.

tcp-socket-short-io.rationale: No maths or code; rules and exception table are procedural; keepalive 7,200 s checked in ip-sysctl. No analogy: a list of API rules gains nothing from a comparison.

tcp-length-prefixed-service.rationale: Big-endian decode is reference (00 00 01 00 = 256 checked with struct). Helpers, threaded server and client executed end to end (b'HELLO'); q7 returns b'abc' leaving b'def'; 0xFFFFFFFF prefix rejected; q5 short header raises 'unpack requires a buffer of 4 bytes'. No analogy: the code is the objective and the previous lesson's dictation analogy covers length prefixes.

questionsRewritten.tcp-sockets-q7: Byte-weight formula card replaced by prose decoding.

tcp-readiness-asyncio.rationale: No maths. Faulty selectors loop and asyncio echo executed on both platforms: small echo works; under a slow reader the selectors loop dies with BlockingIOError (q10). Questions unchanged. No analogy: debugging code paths is the objective.

tcp-cumulative-ack-model.rationale: No maths. rx() executed on Python 3.14 (macOS) and 3.12 (Linux): output matches the lesson and q4 (501/501/1501/2001, 1001 held once). Serial-story analogy maps cumulative ACK/duplicate ACKs; limit mentions bytes and SACK.

tcp-sack-received-ranges.rationale: Option-length card folded into prose: 2 + 4 × 8 = 34 ≤ 40, five blocks 42, three blocks 26 within the 28 left after timestamps. Questions unchanged. No analogy: the lesson is a short extension of the serial-story picture in the previous unit; another comparison would repeat it.

tcp-rto-estimator.rationale: RTO = SRTT + max(G, 4 RTTVAR) kept essential: it is the RFC 6298 definition the lesson and q5 turn on. EWMA updates are reference with a standalone In words line; 300 → 272.5 ms example recomputed. q5 re-derived by simulation: alternating 98/102 ms settles at ≈108.5 ms, alternating 60/140 ms at 268–273 ms, but evenly spread 60–140 ms samples give only ≈140–200 ms, so the prompt now says the samples alternate and the worked example states that assumption. No analogy: the steady/jittery/slowing-path bullets already give the intuition.

tcp-rto-backoff-ambiguity.rationale: Geometric-sum card removed; 0.3+0.6+1.2+2.4 = 4.5 s and 'each wait exceeds all previous waits' checked. tcp_retries2 15 ≈ 924.6 s (a lower bound), tcp_rto_max_ms 120,000 and rto_min 200 ms checked in ip-sysctl; TCP_USER_TIMEOUT semantics in tcp(7). q7 workedExample-only; q9 diagnoses the backoff signature. No analogy: a concrete capture signature carries the idea.

tcp-fast-retransmit-limits.rationale: Summary/reading only changed; no formulas. Questions unchanged and consistent. No analogy: the duplicate-ACK idea is covered by the serial-story analogy two lessons earlier.

tcp-rack-tail-probes.rationale: PTO = 2 × SRTT card removed; 2 × 40 = 80 ms stated in prose and table (RFC 8985 §7.2). q11 workedExample-only change rechecked against RFC 8985. No analogy: the mechanism table is the clearest summary and the lesson is already dense.

tcp-receive-window-budget.rationale: A = max(0, min(rwnd, cwnd) − F) kept essential: the new-data budget is the lesson objective and is needed for q11. Example 14,600 − 10,000 = 4,600 bytes and q11's 40 × 1,460 = 58,400 bytes, ≈28 KB budget recomputed. q2 workedExample-only. Kitchen-pass analogy maps rwnd/recv()/backpressure; limit notes delay and the separate congestion window.

tcp-window-throughput-scaling.rationale: X ≤ W / RTT kept essential (objective; q1/q9). BDP = C RTT and W = F × 2^S are reference cards with standalone In words lines. Recomputed: 65,535 B / 0.1 s ≈ 5.24 Mbit/s and ≈52 Mbit/s at 10 ms; 12.5 MB BDP and ≈0.5 %; 65,535 × 2^14 = 1,073,725,440 B; shift 10 ≈ 67 MB, 11 ≈ 134 MB. Conveyor analogy fair; limit notes variable RTT and two windows.

tcp-buffer-autotuning.rationale: Card removed; 6,000,000 × 8 / 0.1 = 480 Mbit/s and 10^10 × 0.1 / 8 = 125 MB stated in prose. tcp_rmem default 131,072 and SO_RCVBUF disabling autotuning checked. q7 workedExample-only: 65,536 × 8 / 0.12 ≈ 4.4 Mbit/s. No analogy: a diagnostic checklist lesson; the conveyor analogy in the previous unit already covers windows.

tcp-zero-window-syndrome.rationale: Efficiency (10/(10+40)) and Clark threshold cards removed; prose states four-fifths overhead and min(MSS, half buffer) in words, consistent with RFC 9293 §3.8.6.2.2. Questions unchanged. Warehouse analogy maps zero window, lost window update and persist probes; limit notes exponential probe backoff.

tcp-nagle-delayed-acks.rationale: 41-byte and 2 × RMSS cards removed; RFC 9293 <0.5 s and every-second-segment rule rechecked. Moved the fact that Nagle never holds full-sized segments back into the visible text: the author had placed it only inside the collapsed analogy, and tcp-flow-control-q6 option 1 depends on it. Letters analogy maps Nagle and delayed ACK.

tcp-split-write-latency.rationale: No maths. send_request executed: TCP_NODELAY set and peer received header+body in one read. Questions unchanged. No analogy: the trace diagram is the explanation, and the preceding lesson's letters analogy already sets up the interaction.

tcp-congestion-window-model.rationale: X ≈ cwnd / RTT is reference (the same relationship is essential in tcp-window-throughput-scaling); 100 × 1,460 / 0.05 ≈ 23.4 Mbit/s recomputed. q2 diagnoses a halved rate at constant cwnd (RTT doubled). 1986 32 kbit/s → 40 bit/s collapse inherited from the earlier verified record. Redial analogy fair; limit notes inferred signals and lack of central admission.

tcp-slow-start-flights.rationale: IW formula is reference (RFC 6928 text checked); doubling/segment-count cards removed. q1 key holds, but a new connection normally starts with a very high ssthresh (RFC 5681), so the worked example now explains a loss-free exit at 80 by a cached/route ssthresh or Linux CUBIC HyStart, which sets ssthresh to cwnd (tcp_cubic.c v6.12). Café analogy mapping reworded so leftovers are the signal that ends doubling rather than ssthresh itself.

tcp-aimd-reno-recovery.rationale: AIMD pair is reference; substitution replaced by a duplicate-ACK vs RTO table, checked against RFC 5681 (ssthresh ≤ max(FlightSize/2, 2 SMSS), cwnd = ssthresh + 3 SMSS, LW = 1 SMSS). q4 key and the 0.7 CUBIC distractor rechecked. Road analogy fair; reworded 'Chiu–Jain convergence', which opened a routing-convergence entry.

tcp-reno-round-trace.rationale: reno() executed on both platforms; output matches the table, bars and q6 ('4 9 9'). Average-window card replaced by reading guidance (3/4 of peak stated in words). Corrected 'ssthresh is halved' after a timeout (17 → 10 is half the 20-segment window, not half of ssthresh); same wording fixed in q5's explanation. No analogy: tracing the code is the objective.

tcp-reno-large-path-recovery.rationale: T_rec = (W/2) × RTT is reference; 83,333 segments, 41,667 × 0.1 s ≈ 69 min and RFC 3649's 5 × 10^9 packets / 1⅔ hours checked in the RFC. q9 sawtooth re-derived (peak P with P/2 + 6,000 = P gives 12,000; average 9,000 segments ≈ 1.1 Gbit/s); the worked example now states the steady-loss, fast-recovery-only assumptions. No analogy: the road analogy in tcp-aimd-reno-recovery covers AIMD; this is a scaling consequence.

tcp-cubic-time-target.rationale: W(t)/K card is reference; RFC 9438 C = 0.4, β = 0.7. Table recomputed (K = ∛75 ≈ 4.217 s; 70.0, 86.7, 95.6, 100, 102.3, 108.6). q8 trace (cut to 140, K ≈ 5.3 s) consistent. Go-kart analogy fair; limit notes fixed time function and moving share.

tcp-bbr-versioned-model.rationale: BDP/pacing/cap card is reference; 12.5 MB/s × 0.02 s = 250 KB. BBRv1 constants rechecked in Linux v6.12 tcp_bbr.c (2.885 high gain, 5/4 and 3/4 cycle, cwnd gain 2, 10-round bw filter, 10 s min-RTT window, 200 ms ProbeRTT, 4-packet floor, 3 rounds/25 % startup exit). Removed a duplicated sentence; analogy title aligned with its café-manager text.

tcp-ecn-congestion-feedback.rationale: DCTCP update is reference; RFC 8257 g = 1/16 and cwnd × (1 − α/2) checked. Question unchanged. Sticker analogy: title matched to body; limit extended to on-path devices that clear ECN bits (author's low-confidence item).

tcp-short-transfer-timing.rationale: Round-trip sum card removed (the table totals 5 RTTs); 69 segments in flights 10/20/39 rechecked. q1 diagnoses 3 × 50 ms setup-bound calls; 10 KB fits IW10; serialisation ≈80 µs at 1 Gbit/s. No analogy: counting round trips is a short procedure.

tcp-mathis-loss-model.rationale: Mathis approximation kept essential: the square-root law is the objective and q4 supplies it. Derivation and substitution cards removed; 14.2 and 1.42 Mbit/s rechecked; q4 (link capacity absent, <2 % utilisation) and q5 (1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8; 71 → ≈8.9) rechecked. No analogy: the sawtooth explanation is already the intuition.

tcp-bufferbloat-aqm.rationale: Reclassified T_q = Q / R from essential to reference: the sentence before it already states the relationship in words, so seeing the equation is not necessary. 262,144 × 8 / 2 × 10^6 ≈ 1.05 s rechecked. q6 now states the single FIFO queue assumption behind 'roughly doubles'; CoDel q8 control law (interval/√count) matches RFC 8289. Shop-till analogy fair.

tcp-stream-blocking-ossification.rationale: No maths; questions unchanged. Checkout-belt analogy maps HTTP/2 head-of-line blocking; QUIC limit (shared congestion and flow control) accurate.

tcp-quic-transport-tradeoffs.rationale: No maths; questions unchanged. Case-reference analogy: connection IDs, path validation and fresh CIDs on a new path checked in RFC 9000 §9.

tcp-stream-message-framing.rationale: No maths; questions unchanged. Dictation analogy maps byte stream, invisible send() boundaries, delimiters and length prefixes.

tcp-socket-short-io.rationale: No maths or code; rules and exception table are procedural; keepalive 7,200 s checked in ip-sysctl. No analogy: a list of API rules gains nothing from a comparison.
